sections.h2: Why Do Saudi Businesses Choose ERPNext?

paragraphs.text: ERPNext is an open-source ERP with no licence fee per user, covering accounts, stock, buying, selling, manufacturing, projects and HR in one system. For Saudi companies, it also supports Arabic and English side by side, SAR and foreign currencies, and direct integration with ZATCA. A typical Saudi implementation takes 8–12 weeks for a single company and 12–16 weeks for multi-branch groups.

As an ERPNext implementation company Saudi Arabia firms can reach during their working day, we start every project with tax and compliance. Our ERPNext implementation Saudi Arabia projects are planned around your ZATCA wave, your Zakat year and your payroll cycle.

sections.h2: Saudi VAT and Compliance in ERPNext
sections.intro: ERPNext 15% VAT setup follows ZATCA rules from day one:

items.text: Standard rate of 15%, with zero-rated and exempt supplies as separate tax templates
Standard tax invoices for B2B sales and simplified tax invoices for B2C sales
Reverse charge on imported services, posted automatically
VAT return figures prepared box by box for filing on the ZATCA portal
Arabic on invoices, with the seller's and buyer's VAT numbers

paragraphs.text: ZATCA's Phase 2 connects your invoicing system directly to the Fatoora platform. Standard invoices must be cleared before you share them, and simplified invoices must be reported within 24 hours. The latest wave, Wave 25, covers VAT-able revenue above SAR 187,500 and must integrate by 1 February 2027.

paragraphs.html: We handle onboarding, XML invoices, QR codes and rejected-invoice fixes. For the full process, see ERPNext ZATCA e-invoicing. An ERPNext implementation company Saudi Arabia buyers hire should plan ZATCA as part of setup, not as an afterthought.

sections.h2: Zakat, Corporate Tax and Audit Records

paragraphs.text: Saudi and GCC-owned businesses pay Zakat, while the foreign-owned share of a company pays corporate income tax. Mixed-ownership companies deal with both. ERPNext Zakat setup tags the accounts that form your Zakat base, such as equity, long-term liabilities and fixed assets, so your adviser can prepare the return without re-working your books.
We also set up cost centres, related-party tags and audit-ready reports, so year-end and external audits move faster. Every entry keeps a full history of who changed what and when.

Saudi customers, government buyers and banks expect Arabic. We design bilingual Arabic and English invoices, quotations, delivery notes and statements, with Arabic laid out from right to left. Hijri dates can appear alongside Gregorian dates on documents and reports where your customers expect them.
Staff can switch the ERPNext screen language between Arabic and English for each user, so warehouse teams, accountants and managers each work in the language they read fastest.

paragraphs.html: ERPNext's HR app handles attendance, leave, salary components and end-of-service awards under Saudi labour law. It tracks GOSI contributions for Saudi and non-Saudi staff and produces salary files for the Mudad Wage Protection System. Saudization reports help you track nationality mix against your Nitaqat targets. For the full setup, see ERPNext HR and payroll for the GCC.

Many Saudi businesses run branches or warehouses in several cities. Each branch can have its own stock, cost centre and invoicing unit for ZATCA, while management sees one combined view. We move customers, suppliers, items, opening balances and open invoices, with VAT numbers and addresses checked for every record, because ZATCA rejects invoices with missing buyer details. Your old system stays live until the trial balance matches. An ERPNext implementation company Saudi Arabia finance teams trust should treat this as an accounting task, and ours ends with a signed balance check. See ERPNext data migration.

paragraphs.text: Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 programme is pushing businesses toward digital invoicing, digital payroll and cleaner financial records. Banks, investors and government buyers increasingly expect audit-ready books. ERPNext gives growing companies that discipline without the licence costs of large enterprise systems, and it scales from one branch to many.
